content.title: Plan: apply waitForResponse fix to sibling parent-selector test

content.content:
Confirmed fix approach against the actual code in packages/webapp/e2e/phase3-validation.spec.ts.

Verified the defect: "sets a parent via search and selection" (lines 1235-1285) still uses the OLD flaky pattern:
- Lines 1256-1262: `searchInput.fill("Set Parent Target")` runs FIRST, then `page.waitForResponse(...)` is registered AFTER. A fast search response can resolve before the listener attaches.
- The matcher (line 1260) only checks `resp.url().includes("/api/issues")` AND `includes("search=")` — no method pin and no scoping to the exact search term, so it can latch onto an unrelated GET.

Verified the target pattern: the sibling "changes an existing parent" (lines 1326-1335) already uses the fixed recipe:
- `searchResponsePromise = page.waitForResponse(matcher)` is assigned BEFORE `searchInput.fill("New Parent")`, then awaited.
- Matcher pins `method === "GET"`, URL on `/api/issues`, and `new URL(resp.url()).searchParams.get("search") === "New Parent"`.

Confirmed scope for Dev (mqgzjuwgpw): in "sets a parent via search and selection", hoist a `searchResponsePromise` ABOVE the `searchInput.fill("Set Parent Target")` call (lines 1256-1262), scope the matcher to method GET + issues endpoint + `new URL(resp.url()).searchParams.get("search") === "Set Parent Target"`, then `await searchResponsePromise` after the fill. Mechanical change, low risk.

Audit: confirmed the review's file audit — no other search-response attach-order anti-patterns exist in the file (e.g. tree-expand wait at ~line 1029 correctly registers the promise before the triggering click; other waits pair with clicks and set the promise up first). Scope stays limited to this one test.
